claim_to_page_mapping.supported: MSL replaces exact probabilities in a log criterion; simulation expectation and the nonlinear log operation must be distinguished.
claim_to_page_mapping.adoption: Motivation for an independently proved Jensen/finite-simulation example; not a universal parameter-bias theorem.

claim_to_page_mapping.supported: Linear simulated moments, simulated scores, and the reciprocal-probability geometric waiting-time construction are explained.
claim_to_page_mapping.adoption: Use explicit moment orthogonality, independent simulation streams and any required differentiation-under-expectation assumptions.

claim_to_page_mapping.supported: The stated simulation design uses independent draws across observations and common random numbers across trial parameter values for each observation. It separates the original sample term, simulation bias and centered simulation noise.
claim_to_page_mapping.adoption: This distinction supports finite or iid original variance calculations; it does not establish an arbitrary common-across-observation simulator law.

claim_to_page_mapping.supported: Rate discussion contrasts an order 1/R bias with simulation noise of order 1/sqrt(NR), and discusses fixed-R moment/score estimation.
claim_to_page_mapping.adoption: Treat as a roadmap contingent on verified expansion, identification, smoothness, moments, uniformity and simulation design; prove the chapter’s bounded law directly.

claim_to_page_mapping.supported: Squared moment residuals supply a numerical criterion.
claim_to_page_mapping.adoption: Zero residual is a solution only when feasible and attained; a local optimizer or a nonzero least-squares minimum is not proof that moment equations have been solved.

cautions.finding: A zero score is an interior necessary first-order condition, not a general equivalence with the global likelihood maximizer. Boundary optima, multiple stationary points and nonconcavity require separate treatment.

The relevant condition is zero cross moments, commonly supplied by a conditional mean restriction. Orthogonality is weaker than independence; a binary-outcome residual can be heteroskedastic and dependent on instruments while conditionally centered. The square inverse IV display is also limited to a conformable identified setup; overidentified GMM is separate.

A Jensen bias in the log criterion is not automatically an equal bias in the parameter estimator. A criterion shift independent of the parameter need not shift its maximizer; unbiased/degenerate special cases prevent a universal fixed-R inconsistency assertion. Zero simulated probabilities can make the log undefined or minus infinity and require an explicit domain.

The reciprocal-probability and probability-derivative simulators need independent streams or a proved zero covariance for their product to be unbiased. The page 244 product sentence does not state that condition locally; page 256 explicitly requires independent simulation for instruments and the residual probability. Differentiating an unbiased simulator also requires a justified derivative/expectation interchange; linearity alone is insufficient.

The CLT discussion is informal. A sample mean does have a degenerate limiting law under an LLN; approximate finite-sample normality is not an exact law. Independent nonidentical observations need a variance limit and a Lindeberg/Lyapunov-type condition, not merely equal means and finite individual variances.

The generic vector covariance is printed as D_inverse W D_inverse. For a nonsymmetric moment Jacobian it must be D_inverse W D_inverse_transpose. A symmetric likelihood Hessian is a special case. The same qualification applies to the simulation covariance display.

First- and second-order Taylor equalities are written without remainders or intermediate derivatives. To establish a theorem, first prove consistency and control the expansion remainder uniformly near the selected root. The order 1/R bias/rate comparison is not an exact identity for arbitrary nonlinear simulators.

An exact 1/R simulator variance holds for independent averages of a fixed square-integrable statistic; for nonlinear ratio/log transforms it is generally an asymptotic expansion requiring additional conditions. Summing asymptotic normal components needs a joint limit and their covariance, not only two separate marginal limits.

Efficiency and information-equality statements require a correctly specified regular model and a stated estimator class. Under misspecification or irregular support, use the appropriate sandwich and target; no unconditional efficiency claim is inherited. Slow simulation growth can invalidate the displayed centered root-N law without making every bias-corrected or differently centered inference procedure impossible.

proof_assumptions_to_supply: Specify whether the observed records and per-observation simulation draws are iid/independent, and whether simulations are reused across parameter values or observations.

For a direct moment theorem: a compact parameter domain or an explicit globally solvable equation, identified population target, finite moments, suitable uniform convergence and nonsingular local derivative; distinguish global identification from local rank.
For nonlinear simulation: strict positivity and integrability for logs, a controlled Taylor remainder for rate claims, and explicit treatment of zero estimates.
For original finite simulation contracts, enumerate the actual random variables and calculate bias/variance directly; no asymptotic theorem is needed to certify those finite calculations.
sources.excluded: No general simulation empirical-process theorem, global ML consistency/efficiency theorem, arbitrary GMM estimator theory or complete book review is adopted.

claim_to_page_mapping.supported: Primitives specify costs, transitions, discounting and the agent’s observed state; choices come from dynamic optimization. Observationally unobserved utility shocks belong inside that model.
claim_to_page_mapping.adoption: Context for a new finite-state structural map and value problem, not the paper’s bus data, calibration or estimates.

claim_to_page_mapping.supported: Conditional independence factors next-state and next-shock distributions; the continuation function can be computed on a reduced state/action space.
claim_to_page_mapping.adoption: State this as a maintained law and directly prove the finite-state contraction used by the chapter.

claim_to_page_mapping.supported: With independent extreme-value utility shocks, conditional choice probabilities have a softmax/logit form based on current payoff plus discounted continuation.
claim_to_page_mapping.adoption: Use a fresh explicit shock location/scale normalization and correct expected-max calculation; see printed display cautions.

claim_to_page_mapping.supported: Conditional likelihood factors into observed transitions and conditional choices. NFXP nests a numerical fixed-point solution within parameter search. The footnote explicitly flags discretization error as potentially relevant for statistical asymptotics.
claim_to_page_mapping.adoption: Keep numerical solution error, parameter identification and statistical uncertainty separate.

claim_to_page_mapping.supported: The applied cost level is normalized because a common utility level is not identified; shock location and scale are normalized absent additional information. Footnote 11 discusses possible cross-bus dependence from shared service capacity.
claim_to_page_mapping.adoption: State maintained utility units, discount factor and transitions and test whether observed choice probabilities identify the desired parameter combinations.

cautions.finding: The printed expected-max integrand omits the alternative-specific epsilon_j term. The earlier Bellman and choice rule4.4/4.6 include it. The consistent surplus is E[max_j{u_j+beta EV_j+epsilon_j}]; integrating a deterministic max would not generate the later smooth choice probabilities.

As printed, the unit-scale Gumbel density has location theta2 with theta2=+Euler gamma. Its mean is theta2+gamma, hence 2gamma, while the later text uses zero-mean shocks and equation 4.12 uses pure log-sum-exp. For that zero-mean expected-max normalization, location must be −gamma; alternatively retain the additive mean constant consistently. A common shock-location shift leaves choice probabilities unchanged but changes value levels. This is an independent mathematical qualification of the exact printed density, not an alternative claim about an uninspected version.

General existence, smoothness and estimator asymptotics are referred to other Rust work and regularity conditions; the empirical paper is not a self-contained universal identification/consistency theorem. The paper’s theorem references are not proof prerequisites already discharged by this inspection.

A contraction with beta<1 establishes uniqueness and an error bound for a specified state space. It does not provide uniform good conditioning as beta approaches 1; numerical perturbations can be amplified by 1/(1−beta). A Newton iteration’s local convergence is not guaranteed by treating any arbitrary starting point as safe.

The derivation treats the fixed point as exact. State discretization and fixed-point tolerance can affect the likelihood and inference; finite computational accuracy must be bounded relative to the task and any claimed statistical rate.

Choice data do not automatically identify absolute utility level, shock scale, discounting, transitions and all costs jointly. A normalized or externally calibrated value is a maintained input unless a separate identifying argument is supplied. Independent units and conditional-independence structure cannot be inferred merely from fit.

OCR of the simple exponential-transition example loses mathematical signs and operators. That analytic exponential/threshold/first-passage example is excluded from the chapter’s adopted proof scope rather than transcribed from extracted text.

proof_assumptions_to_supply: For a new finite-state/action model use bounded deterministic rewards, stochastic transition rows, discount 0≤beta<1 and an integrable explicitly normalized iid shock law. Prove the relevant max or log-sum-exp operator is beta-Lipschitz in sup norm.
Give the transition and information law explicitly. A single-agent controlled Markov problem is not automatically a market equilibrium or an equilibrium-selection model.
Separate an inner numerical certificate ||V−Vstar||≤||TV−V||/(1−beta) from global parameter identification and from the outer optimizer’s attainment/uniqueness.
For derivative/sensitivity calculations, prove the stated inverse or implicit derivative exists under the declared finite model; do not infer it from a computer solver’s convergence flag.
sources.excluded: No bus data, estimates, original empirical tables or exercises will be copied. No empirical-fit validation, general dynamic-choice identification, arbitrary dependent-data likelihood CLT, companion-paper theorem or global Newton convergence claim is adopted.

claim_to_page_mapping.pages: Physical 4–6 / printed S87–S89, equations 3–11 and assumption A4
claim_to_page_mapping.supported: The auxiliary estimator targets a binding function determined by the structural law and auxiliary criterion; matching observed and simulated auxiliary estimates is a minimum-distance procedure. The paper separately assumes global one-to-one binding and a full-column-rank derivative.
claim_to_page_mapping.adoption: Use an explicitly derived finite binding map, prove injectivity or exhibit its identified set, and assess derivative sensitivity separately.

claim_to_page_mapping.supported: H simulation paths use independent innovation draws, while all parameter trials reuse their simulation seeds; an alternative stacks a longer simulated path with a repeated exogenous sequence.
claim_to_page_mapping.adoption: Specify the chapter’s data and simulation law exactly. Common random numbers across parameter trials do not mean identical shocks across independent units.

claim_to_page_mapping.pages: Physical 8–9 / printed S91–S92, assumptions A5–A8, equations 14–19, propositions3–4
claim_to_page_mapping.supported: A joint asymptotic normal law for the observed-minus-simulated auxiliary score is assumed. Additional covariance/Hessian limits and regularity enter the estimator law. Under the stated shared-exogenous-path construction, the variance contains I0−K0 and a factor 1+1/H.
claim_to_page_mapping.adoption: Prove a narrower iid or finite simulation law directly; do not inherit a generic time-series CLT from stationarity.

claim_to_page_mapping.pages: Physical 10 / printed S93 and physical 26 / printed S109
claim_to_page_mapping.supported: The source warns that its infinite-H covariance is not generally the covariance obtained using the population binding function when exogenous variables are present. The appendix derives the observed-minus-average-simulated covariance and its shared-path cancellation.
claim_to_page_mapping.adoption: Keep actual and simulated sample sizes, conditional common inputs and their covariance in the original calculation.

cautions.finding: Auxiliary consistency and indirect-estimator consistency require a uniform limit and an identified/separated optimum, not a visual fit or a single convergent optimizer run. Local rank does not imply global injectivity; the source’s A4 explicitly requires both.

The discussion treats conditioning on the observed exogenous path as requiring strong exogeneity. Its broad sentence about non-strongly-exogenous variables being nonsimulable is not adopted literally: jointly modeling and simulating endogenous state variables is possible, but requires a different complete law.

When structural and auxiliary dimensions match, weighting can drop out only if the binding equations are solvable at an admissible parameter and the selected solution is appropriate. On a constrained domain or under misspecification, an equal-dimensional minimum-distance optimum need not attain zero and can depend on weights.

Assumption A5 supplies a joint score-difference CLT; assumptions A6–A8 supply covariance and Hessian limits. These are not proved merely by stating a stationary Markov model. Proposition 3 also retains usual regularity conditions, so the chapter must provide explicit sufficient conditions for its own law.

cautions.pages: S92–S93 and S109, actual equation pages S92/S109 checked
cautions.finding: The factor 1+1/H arises from the specified independent simulated paths relative to a sample-length-T observed process, conditional on shared exogenous values. I0−K0 captures conditional rather than total score noise. Another design with simulation length S, common observation shocks or reestimated shared inputs needs its own covariance calculation.

The inverse weighting formula requires invertibility/positive definiteness on the moment space and a full-rank binding Jacobian. A singular moment covariance or unidentified direction cannot be silently inverted.

The selected appendix uses local first-order expansions around a consistent estimator. The inspection does not supply a complete global consistency or dependent-data empirical-process proof; remainder control and the initial-condition/neighborhood limits must be stated if used.

OCR deletes some displayed equations and confuses theta, beta, transpose marks and hats. The four retained equation-page images are the authority for their exact inspected displays; unviewed equations are not copied into a proof.

proof_assumptions_to_supply: Define structural parameter domain, auxiliary population target b(theta), observed auxiliary estimator and simulated counterpart before comparing them. Give a globally injective map or an explicit nonidentification example, then state local derivative conditions separately.

A bounded iid direct proof can derive the joint limit of independent observed and simulated auxiliary moments from the accepted iid CLT; its covariance is the sum of correctly scaled terms plus any stated cross covariance.

For an affine full-rank binding map, solve weighted minimum distance exactly and derive its covariance; for a nonlinear map, independently establish consistency, a local derivative expansion and remainder control.
Hold the simulator’s parameter-indexed draws fixed during optimization for the stated sample objective, and distinguish finite simulation randomness from repeated sampling.
sources.excluded: No Monte Carlo examples, applications, hypotheses/specification tests, optimal-inference theorem beyond the inspected assumptions, complete appendices or general simulation-based dependent-data CLT claimed verified.

proof_route_suggestions.route: Derive the observable mapping from stated behavioral/equilibrium equations first. Compare multiple primitive vectors for observational equivalence. Treat a fixed discount, shock scale or omitted supply parameter as a maintained/calibrated input until a data-based identifying argument is given. A parameter chosen to match one moment can be an estimator only relative to a stated sampling law and identifying restriction.
proof_route_suggestions.source_relation: The three sources motivate model-to-data maps and maintained primitives; the original finite identification or nonidentification proof remains the coordinator’s task.

proof_route_suggestions.topic: Finite-state dynamic choice and numerical certification
proof_route_suggestions.route: For finite states/actions and beta<1, bound the difference of two max/log-sum-exp values by the maximum difference in their choice indices. Stochastic transition rows then make the Bellman operator a beta-contraction. A Cauchy/geometric argument gives a unique value; a residual divided by 1−beta bounds numerical error. State the Gumbel location explicitly, keeping any expected-max constant. Prove probability/log-likelihood perturbation bounds only for the declared finite domain.
proof_route_suggestions.source_relation: A restricted self-contained counterpart to Rust’s NFXP architecture, not a claim that an inner fixed point identifies outer parameters or proves a market equilibrium.

proof_route_suggestions.route: Use a directly specified affine moment equation or a finite simulator. Derive sampling and simulation errors as explicit sums. Independent simulation by observation averages differently from one shared shock reused for every observation. Common random numbers across parameter trials define an optimization objective but do not automatically remove Monte Carlo variance.
proof_route_suggestions.source_relation: Train explicitly states independent observation simulations and same draws across parameter values. GMR’s shared exogenous paths explain why covariance terms must be tracked.

proof_route_suggestions.route: Prove Jensen’s log inequality under strict positivity/integrability, and calculate the actual expected simulated criterion in a bounded example. Examine its maximizer instead of equating criterion bias with parameter bias. If an estimator is nonlinear, derive its finite law or a remainder-controlled expansion.
proof_route_suggestions.source_relation: Original derivation supplies the missing distinction behind Train’s heuristic bias/rate discussion; no fixed-R universal inconsistency statement is inherited.

proof_route_suggestions.route: Choose an explicit auxiliary binding map. For an affine full-column-rank map, solve the weighted normal equations and derive exact covariance under an explicit observed/simulated Gaussian or iid limit law. Exhibit global noninjectivity even when a local derivative is nonzero if relevant. Perturb both observed moments and maintained model inputs through the stated Jacobian, separating numerical conditioning from identification.
proof_route_suggestions.source_relation: Use the GMR binding/minimum-distance architecture, but prove the actual map, sampling law, simulation-length scaling and restrictions independently.

remaining_scope_gaps: The three bodies do not provide a fully inspected self-contained general equilibrium existence/selection theorem. Any original equilibrium example must state its own model and prove its finite solution/selection rule.
No general dependent-data simulation CLT, arbitrary structural identification theorem, uniformly valid inference procedure or globally convergent outer optimizer is supplied by this preparation.
The original Rust companion theorem and modern extensions, Train’s other chapters and GMR’s remaining testing/application/appendix material are outside this inspection.
Numerical blueprint and subsequent complete original proofs, examples, solutions and review gates belong to a separate author assignment.
inventory_policy: Every file currently within the assigned scratch subtree is listed by exact path relative to book, bytes and SHA256. Sources remain scratch/reference artifacts, not reader attachments or shared source-catalogue mutations.
limits: Method sources and limited equation corrections do not verify a real structural model, causal interpretation, empirical estimates or external validity.
Original proof-route suggestions are not attributed as complete source theorems.
Machine-assisted preparation is not independent human certification; chapter acceptance is separate.

final_validation.method: Independent standard-library strict JSON/hash/inventory checks and existing pdfinfo page counts; source prose spacing clarified before freeze.
final_validation.limitations: These artifact checks confirm provenance and declared scope. They do not substitute for the actual textual/equation reading or a later independent chapter review.
